## Summary

The tweet presents the **APMEM\* Signal System** — SPY long/short signals driven by a volatility forecast — and gives its call for Tuesday, November 10, 2026: **LONG SPY**.

- **The engine:** APEM/MEM-class volatility forecasting "straight out of the NYU Lab handbook." The dashboard confirms the citation: Engle, R.F. (2002), *New Frontiers for ARCH Models*, J. Applied Econometrics 17: 425–446 — NYU Stern V-Lab. APMEM = Asymmetric Power Multiplicative Error Model.
- **The signal construction (from the full fxtwitter text):** a "bottom watch" and "top watch" that are **hybrid/coincident signals** — the APMEM volatility forecast must agree with Signal Sigma's bullish/bearish options conditions for a long or short to fire.
- **The dashboard (rendered + OCR):** title "APMEM\* Signal System — SPY Volatility Regime Long & Short Signals", "Volatility prediction for Tuesday, November 10th, 2026", verdict **LONG SPY**. ## Skepticism gates

Self-reported returns with no stated methodology for the performance stats (unknown whether 21.83% 1D is model-return, signal-hit-rate, or a cherry-picked window; no drawdown, no baseline comparison, no cost model). "High performance in OOS testing for 3 years" is a claim, not a receipt — no backtest package, code drop, or trade log is linked (contrast the Milk Man receipt culture). The hybrid gating (APMEM × Signal Sigma conditions) is described but not specified — coincident indicators can be fit to the same history, so OOS discipline is unverifiable from outside. AI-assisted build ("Claude Opus 5.5" credit) is novel transparency but says nothing about out-of-sample validity. 32 likes / 3.5k views = low distribution today; today's LONG call is the first independently checkable data point.
